headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared OAuth/API surfaces create plausible leakage and conflict paths, while prompt-injection risk is low and compliance risk is limited by absent sensitive-data evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth2 and ForwardAuth, while Superset exposes a Superset API; no shared channel or parser is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual or indirect content transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies Authelia-generated content into Superset configuration or prompts
IF Superset ingests Authelia output through a shared file or message channel
mitigations: Disable copy-paste bridges between the two systems during review
Require human review of any Authelia-generated text before Superset consumes it
Use separate workspaces for configuration artifacts
Log and diff any transferred content before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth2 flows; Superset has allowlisted egress and a Superset API. No sensitive data classes are listed, but a shared workspace or token flow could move data between them in default deployments, so leakage is plausible though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or identity provider
IF Authelia forwards identity or session material into Superset-visible logs or API payloads
mitigations: Separate credentials and service accounts for each agent
Restrict Authelia egress to only required IdP endpoints
Turn off verbose request logging on both systems
Review API payloads for tokens or identifiers before enabling integration

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make broad outbound requests and Superset can make allowlisted outbound requests, so overlapping mutable network behavior exists. Neither profile shows filesystem writes or locking, but shared OAuth/identity resources can still conflict if both are pointed at the same backend.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same identity or API-backed resource
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes to shared configuration
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials to each agent
Serialize any shared-resource updates through one operator
Freeze configuration changes during rollout windows
Add a simple lock file or change window for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and Superset can consume API-driven configuration or data. If Superset treats Authelia output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into downstream actions; no verification mechanism is documented in either profile, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF Superset consumes Authelia-derived claims or decisions without independent verification
IF an authentication or authorization error is propagated into a downstream dashboard or API action
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Superset acts on Authelia output
Require explicit approval for any downstream action based on identity claims
Add alerting for unexpected auth-state changes
Keep a rollback path for any configuration derived from upstream output

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no touched data classes, certifications, or residency constraints. With no evidence of regulated data flow, compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway, and the other agent is not separately implicated.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not present in the profiles
mitigations: Confirm whether any regulated data will traverse the pair
Document retention and deletion settings for both systems
Keep the pair out of PHI/PII workflows unless controls are added
